# v0.49.90

This patch fixes three ways an outdated checkpoint record could hide messages or refuse a session on OpenCode 2. OpenCode 1 and Pi are not affected and do not change.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: messages could be missing from requests after the history got shorter.** An OpenCode 2 session keeps a record of where the stored conversation continues after the history block. When the summaries later covered less than that record claimed, the messages in between were sent neither as messages nor as summaries. The store was intact, and nothing told you. We reproduced it three ways: a `/ctx-recomp` that stopped partway after a manual `/compact` (28 messages), a `/ctx-recomp` that stopped partway in a session converted from OpenCode 1 (37 messages), and a completed `/ctx-recomp` followed by a revert in such a session (17 messages). Magic Context now ignores a record that points past the history it rendered, serves the stored messages from the real position, and saves the corrected record on that request. Present since 0.49.47. 0.49.89 already stopped a partial `/ctx-recomp` from shortening the history; this release repairs sessions that are already in that state and covers the other ways into it.
- **OpenCode 2: a session could refuse every turn with `MC-S06` after a revert past its summaries.** The sequence was an early `/compact`, later summaries, a second `/compact`, and a revert that removed the messages those summaries ended on. Now a revert retires the summaries of the messages it removed, and a session with no summaries and no usable record starts again from its first stored message. A session that was already refused before the update still holds its outdated summaries: run `/ctx-recomp` to the end once, and it serves turns again.

## What to expect after the update

- **One prompt rebuild per affected session.** The first request after the correction rebuilds the cached prompt once. In a session that was refused on every turn and still has summaries, the second request changes once more, because one host instruction line is now covered by a summary. Magic Context logs that change once.
- **Restored messages can appear as `[dropped §N§]`.** Messages that were marked as no longer needed before the history got shorter stay reduced. They come back as placeholders, or stay left out where an earlier cleanup had removed the message from the request, until a summary covers them again. `ctx_expand` with the tag or the message still returns the original. Search and range `ctx_expand` treat these messages as visible; that is a known limit and not new in this release.
- **A large session may refuse one or two turns while it catches up.** In our test, a session with 75,000 tokens of unsummarized messages in a 60,000-token window was refused for two turns while summaries were written, and served at 55,700 tokens on the third. No command or restart was needed.
- **One limit.** The proof that a revert removed a message is kept in memory, from the revert on. So two kinds of session can keep the `MC-S06` refusal: one that was refused before the update, and one whose host restarted right after the revert while a summary run was still in progress. Run `/ctx-recomp` to the end to clear it.
- **Healthy sessions do not change.** On OpenCode 2.0.22, 2.1.0, 2.3.2 and 2.4.2, requests of sessions without this damage are byte-identical with and without this fix.

# v0.49.89

This patch changes what a `/ctx-recomp` that stops partway does, and it protects a data folder that is a symbolic link.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Changed

- **A `/ctx-recomp` that stops partway now keeps your current history.** Before, a full rebuild that failed partway replaced the old summaries with the part it had finished. The messages behind that part lost their summaries. On OpenCode 2, after a manual `/compact`, those messages could be missing from later requests until the rebuild was run to the end (28 messages in our test). Now a stopped rebuild publishes nothing unless it already covers everything the current summaries cover. The result is headed "Paused", says how far the rebuild got, and says that your history is unchanged. The next `/ctx-recomp` continues from that point and does not send the finished part to the model again. This holds on OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2 and Pi.
- **A rebuild that cannot get past one point is discarded, not repeated forever.** If a resumed rebuild stops again at the same message, with the same input and no model failure in between, Magic Context discards the unfinished part and says so. Your current history stays as it is. A model or provider failure never causes a discard; such a rebuild stays paused.
- **`/ctx-recomp` with a range refuses while a full rebuild is paused.** It tells you to run `/ctx-recomp` without arguments first. A full rebuild started while a range rebuild is unfinished discards the range leftovers and starts from the first message.
- **A data folder that is a symbolic link is now made owner-only at its target.** Earlier releases opened a linked data folder, but the check that makes the store private skipped it without a message. Magic Context now follows the link and makes the target folder private (`0700` for directories, `0600` for files), unless you turned owner-only storage off. It does this only when the target is not a filesystem root, your home folder or a mount point, and holds nothing but Magic Context's own files. If the target holds anything else, Magic Context leaves its permissions alone and logs how many foreign entries it found. Give the store a folder of its own so it can be protected. Links inside the data folder are not followed, and a broken link does not stop the host from starting. The configuration reference describes the rule below the `storage` settings.

## Fixed

- **A rebuild that reached the end of what can be summarized was reported as partial.** When only messages with nothing to summarize remained, `/ctx-recomp` reported a partial result and asked you to run it again. It now completes, keeps the later summaries as they are, and says which messages stay as they are.
- **`/ctx-recomp` on a session whose messages are all still in the recent raw part said it had lost a lock.** It now says there is nothing to rebuild yet.

# v0.49.87

This patch fixes seven faults on OpenCode 2, OpenCode 1 and Pi, and makes automatic search answer in time after a pause. Most of the faults were found by running end-to-end tests that no CI job had run before.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: a session was refused on every turn after the message that ended its newest summary was deleted** (error `MC-S06`). Magic Context removed the broken summary and scheduled a rebuild, but a second check on the host's own checkpoint ran first and refused the turn, on every later turn too. The session now continues from the newest summary that is still intact. The messages after it are sent in full until they are summarized again. If the first turn after the repair fails for another reason, such as a busy store, the next turn still recovers. On the turn after a recovery, one host instruction line that the summary covers (for example a date change) can leave the request. That costs one prompt-cache write, once, and Magic Context logs it.
- **OpenCode 2.3 and 2.4: a request could exceed the model's context window in a session that Magic Context had not summarized yet.** The last size check before sending did not count the session's tool definitions when the host recorded them under an agent name. In our test that hid about 5,000 tokens, and a 61,184-token request went to a 60,000-token window. The check now counts the tool list that the session's own last request carried, and prefers it over an older stored figure for the same model.
- **OpenCode 2.1 and later: a background run that hit the model's output limit lost its explanation.** These hosts retry such an answer twice and then report a plain failure, so Magic Context treated it as a generic error. It now records the run as cut off by the output limit, as it does on OpenCode 2.0. The token count of a run with several steps now includes every step and leaves out the host's automatic repeats.
- **OpenCode 1 and 2: the task that learns from user friction accepted an answer that was cut off by the output limit.** It then moved its position forward, so the messages behind the cut were never looked at. A cut-off answer now fails the run, and the next run reads the same messages again.
- **OpenCode 1: a maintenance run that reached its token budget could lose all of its results.** When the budget is reached, Magic Context refuses further tool calls and asks the model to wrap up. Tool calls that the model had issued just before were refused too, and the second refusal ended the run before the wrap-up request reached the model. Calls that were already running are now spared once, and the run ends only on a refusal after the wrap-up request.
- **Pi: the same loss of results in a maintenance run at its budget.** The fix is the same. It does not depend on the wording of the wrap-up request, because a Pi extension can change that text.
- **OpenCode 1: a turn that Magic Context refused showed only "Unexpected server error".** OpenCode 1 replaces a plugin's error text with a generic one. Magic Context now also shows its own explanation as a notice in the terminal that has the session open, for 15 seconds. OpenCode's web app and SDK callers still see the generic text.
- **Automatic search often timed out on the first turn after a pause** (issue 773). The search worker stopped five minutes after its last search, so the next turn started a new one and loaded its vectors within the one-second limit. The worker now stays for as long as the session's prompt cache lives after the last reply (at least five minutes, at most one hour), keeps its memory vectors loaded, and checks at most once a minute whether the store changed. A newly started worker now answers first and loads history vectors afterwards. In our measurement, the first search after a ten-minute pause took 23 ms, down from 134 ms, with identical results. Th

# v0.49.86

This patch fixes a crash of the Magic Context sidebar in the OpenCode terminal, and makes the nightly memory check cover code inside git submodules.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode terminal: the sidebar could crash after a status refresh** (issue 987, thanks @iceteaSA for the report and the fix). The sidebar read some status values without checking that they were present. When a refresh delivered a status without one of them, the sidebar crashed. It now checks every status value before it uses it and leaves out a part whose value is missing.
- **The nightly memory check skipped memories about code in git submodules** (issue 973, thanks @AyhamJo7 for the fix). To check a memory against the code, Magic Context lists the files that git tracks. That list did not include files inside submodules, so a memory about such a file was never checked, while the run still reported itself as complete. The list now includes the files of submodules. This applies to OpenCode, Pi and Oh My Pi.

# v0.49.85

This patch fixes a crash at exit on Pi that could happen while a local embedding was being computed, and makes startup faster for stores with many files.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Pi: the process could abort at exit while a local embedding was running** (issue 995, thanks @chpock). With the local embedding provider, Magic Context computes embeddings in a worker that calls a native library. When Pi shut down, Magic Context stopped that worker at once, also in the middle of a native call, and Pi's shutdown did not wait for it. Under Node the process then ended with `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'Napi::Error'` and exit code 134 in place of a normal exit. In our reproduction on Node 26 this happened in 18 of 20 exits that had an embedding in flight. Now stopping the worker is a request. The worker finishes the call it is running, starts no further one, releases the model and ends by itself, and Pi's shutdown waits for that. The wait was 10 to 310 ms in the test runs. The same holds for a worker that a configuration or model change retired shortly before the exit.
- **Oh My Pi:** the same abort happened on Bun in a few of 20 such exits. It is fixed by the same change.
- **A worker that does not stop is bounded.** If a worker does not end within 5 seconds, it is terminated as before, and a stop always settles within about 7 seconds. One log line says that the worker was terminated and whether an embedding was running.

OpenCode itself was not at risk: there the worker runs in a child process. That child is now asked to stop in the same way and is no longer killed in the middle of a call.

- **Startup checked the permissions of every file in the storage folder, twice** (issue 878, thanks @iceteaSA for the report and the fix). On the first database open in a process, Magic Context checked every entry under its storage folder, on the main thread, two times. A store with thousands of files made startup slow. Now a clean full check leaves a private marker in the storage folder. While the marker is valid, a start checks only the storage folder, the database files and the `models/` and `logs/` folders: 7 file checks in a test fixture that needed 2,004 before. The marker is valid for 24 hours and only when it holds the current rule version. Any wrong mode, an unusable marker, or a start with enforcement off removes it, and the next start does the full check again. A file that becomes readable by others after a clean check is repaired at the next full check, at most 24 hours later. The plugin still skips permission repair on Windows. A storage folder that is a symbolic link is followed as before; the permission check does not follow links, so it reports such a folder in the log and does not skip the full check for it.

## Known limit

An exit that does not go through the host's own shutdown, such as a fatal error or another extension that calls `process.exit`, can still abort under Node when an embedding is running at that moment. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D, `/quit`, SIGTERM and SIGHUP in Pi's interactive mode go through the shutdown and are covered.

## Changed

- When a running embedding worker is stopped, the log has one line with the process id, whether an embedding was running, and how long the stop took: `[magic-context] embedding worker stopped (…)`.
- Embedding results and the speed of a normal embedding request are unchanged.
